# jlbind

Call Julia code from R without starting a Julia session.

jlbind compiles Julia code into a shared library with
[JuliaC.jl](https://github.com/JuliaLang/JuliaC.jl) (by default with
`--trim=safe`), and R calls it through R’s official C API. Thus, there
is almost no overhead (see
[Performance](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/articles/performance.html)).

Several R packages using jlbind can be installed side by side: their
Julia code is compiled into one shared library.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("BjarkeHautop/jlbind")
```

Building the shared library requires [Julia](https://julialang.org) \>=
1.13. Installing jlbind does not itself build the library.

## Using a package built on jlbind

After installing or updating an R package that uses jlbind, build the
shared library:

``` r

jlbind::install_backend()
```

This compiles the Julia code of every installed package that uses jlbind
and may take a few minutes. Run it again whenever you install or update
one of them.

## Writing a package that uses jlbind

Set up a package with
[`jlbind::use_jlbind()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/use_jlbind.md),
then declare the Julia functions R can call in the generated binding
package under `inst/julia/`:

``` julia
module MyPkgBindings

using JLBind

greet(name::String) = "Hello, " * name * "!"
@rcall greet(name::String)::String

end
```

Run
[`jlbind::update_entrypoints()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/update_entrypoints.md),
and call the function from R:

``` r

greet <- function(name) .Call(C_greet, name)
```

See [Writing a package that uses
jlbind](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/articles/writing-clients.html)
for a full walkthrough.

# Package index

## Building the library

Compile the Julia code of the installed packages that use jlbind.

- [`install_backend()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/install_backend.md)
  : Build the Julia library
- [`build_library()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/build_library.md)
  : Build a Julia library from specific packages
- [`jlbind_clients()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/jlbind_clients.md)
  : List the packages that use jlbind

## At run time

Bind a package to the compiled library, and check on it.

- [`bind()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/bind.md) :
  Bind a package to the Julia library
- [`is_bound()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/is_bound.md)
  [`check_backend()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/is_bound.md)
  : Check whether a package is bound to the Julia library
- [`backend_info()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/backend_info.md)
  : Information about the loaded Julia library

## Package development

Set up a package to use jlbind.

- [`use_jlbind()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/use_jlbind.md)
  : Set up a package to use jlbind
- [`update_entrypoints()`](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/reference/update_entrypoints.md)
  : Update the list of Julia functions R can call
